title: A worktree's identity can change after TermAl resolved a shell's place in it (a .git removed or added, a link swapped), and overlap keys stay stale
outcome: TermAl resolves where a shell is, and which worktree that place belongs to (engram_worktree_root, cached for 30 s, and the session's remembered workdir_worktree), when a command starts. A later command can change that identity: `rm -rf sub/.git` moves sub into the parent worktree, `git init` or `git worktree add` makes a new one, and a link or junction swap retargets a path. After that, overlap marking may use a key that no longer names where writes land. On one line with the change, the lost-shell reader of PI-26a now treats such lines as anywhere, and an in-line path change was the Claude reviewer's round-3 Note. Across commands, for followed and lost shells alike, the pre-existing staleness remains.
acceptance: Overlap marking cannot miss a write because a worktree's identity changed after its key was taken: either keys are re-taken when a command that may change paths ends, or such a command marks the session's places as anywhere for the rest of the turn; a regression test covers `rm -rf sub/.git` in one command and a write in sub in the next
